headline: Kai, today turns on 10 a.m. in Jackson Hole, where Kevin Warsh gives his first keynote as Fed chair with a third of bond traders pricing a September hike.
subline: Futures are idling after Nvidia's blowout carried the S&P 500 to 7,731, and core inflation stuck at 3.3% is the number Warsh has to answer for.
asof: Pre-market · Friday ~6:40 AM ET · index rows are overnight futures · every figure links to a source below

items.title: Warsh takes the Jackson Hole podium at 10
items.sentence: Kevin Warsh delivers his first Jackson Hole keynote as Fed chair at 10 a.m. ET, with roughly a third of bond traders pricing a September hike and Cleveland Fed officials calling policy too accommodative, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Futures idle into the speech
items.sentence: S&P 500 futures are off 0.02% at 7,741, with Nasdaq 100 futures down 0.11% and Dow futures up 0.12%, per Investing.com's futures board.

items.title: Also today: Chicago PMI, Michigan sentiment
items.sentence: Chicago PMI prints at 9:45 a.m. and final August Michigan consumer sentiment at 10 — both likely footnotes by the time Warsh clears his throat, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: Ten-year yield firms to 4.68%
items.sentence: The 10-year Treasury yield sits at 4.68% after two straight sessions of gains, up 0.45 points over the past year, per Trading Economics.

items.title: Gold holds $4,612 on the debasement trade
items.sentence: Gold added 0.24% to $4,611.72 as expanded Treasury debt buybacks kept debt-crisis worries — the so-called debasement trade — alive, still below January's $5,608 record, per Trading Economics.

items.title: Bitcoin surges past $80,000, then settles
items.sentence: Bitcoin touched $81,281 overnight and now trades at $79,841, up 6.3% on the week amid strong ETF inflows and institutional demand, per CoinGecko.

items.title: Hormuz deal stops short of reopening
items.sentence: Brent eased 0.47% to $88.10 after Iran and Oman's Hormuz revenue-sharing pact came with no guarantee of an immediate reopening of the strait, per Trading Economics.

items.title: Nepal-Tibet floods kill more than 400
items.sentence: Flash floods along the Nepal-Tibet border have killed more than 400 people and swept away villages, with 90 Americans among the missing, NPR reports.

items.title: US, South Korea and Japan schedule drills
items.sentence: Washington, Seoul and Tokyo announced a trilateral military exercise as North Korea ramps up pressure on the US, NPR reports.

items.title: Ceasefire envoy faults Israel's continued attacks
items.sentence: The official leading the White House's Gaza ceasefire effort warned that continued Israeli attacks threaten the proposed peace plan, NPR reports.

items.title: Ratko Mladic dies in custody at 84
items.sentence: The Bosnian Serb commander who oversaw atrocities in a war that killed more than 100,000 people died in custody at 84, NPR reports.

items.title: Nvidia's answer: up 8.74% on double volume
items.sentence: Nvidia closed up 8.74% at $227.98 on twice its normal volume, dragging the S&P 500 up 0.72% to 7,731 and the Nasdaq up 1.57%, per the Motley Fool.

items.title: AI industry closes ranks on cyber defense
items.sentence: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft and more than 100 other firms called for new cyber defenses, warning that AI-enabled attacks will spread as models improve, TechCrunch reports.

items.title: Software earnings ignite: Salesforce up 20.1%
items.sentence: Salesforce jumped 20.1% and Okta 23.3% in a software-and-cybersecurity surge that left tech the only advancing S&P 500 sector Thursday, per TheStreet.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly eyes $1 trillion debut
items.sentence: OpenAI is reportedly targeting an IPO debut valued above $1 trillion, per the Motley Fool.

items.title: Marvell beats, raises, falls anyway
items.sentence: Marvell dropped more than 7% after hours despite lifting its fiscal 2028 revenue outlook to $18 billion, with investors wanting a wider margin of victory, per SiliconANGLE.
